standard_prerequisites.name: Primes of a tensor product over an algebraic extension are maximal
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the primes whose orbits are studied into maximal ideals, which the Galois action can be compared on.

core_obligations: Reduce to the intermediate subextension supplied by the preceding lemma and note that all the primes in play are maximal, since the separable closure is algebraic over the base (proof lines 11670-11675).

Describe the primes of the small base change as kernels of the maps obtained by composing with the elements of the Galois group, and observe that the action is transitive on them, which transfers to the original base change (proof lines 11676-11695).
proof_roadmap: Pass to the intermediate subextension where the tensor product is a product of fields (proof lines 11670-11675).
Realise the primes as kernels of the Galois translates and conclude transitivity (proof lines 11676-11696).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a field extension K of k and a separable algebraic closure, the absolute Galois group acts transitively on the primes of the base change of K to the closure (statement lines 11662-11668). The proof does not use the theory of the absolute Galois group as a profinite group: it passes to the intermediate subextension where the base change is a product of fields, notes that the relevant primes are maximal because the closure is algebraic, and realises the primes as kernels of the maps obtained by composing with the Galois translates (proof lines 11670-11696). Turning the orbits into kernels of the Galois translates is the step that gives transitivity. H2.
